original.title: fix: prevent stuck power lock when restarting an offline server (k8s)

output.title: Fix stuck power lock when restarting an offline Kubernetes server
output.body:
Restarting or stopping an offline server left the panel stuck with "another power action is currently being processed for this server" for about 10 minutes. A stopped Pod isn't auto-removed, so `Terminate` saw it wasn't running and returned without deleting it, then `WaitForStop` fell into `waitForPodDeletion` and blocked for the full `duration` waiting for a deletion that never comes, holding the power lock the whole time.

- `WaitForStop` in `power.go` now checks the Pod up front: `NotFound` or non-running phase marks the environment offline and returns immediately instead of entering the stop/wait-for-deletion flow.
- Extracted the repeated stopping→offline transition into `markOffline()`, reused by both `WaitForStop` and `Terminate`.
- `Start` still recreates the Pod via `OnBeforeStart`, so no stale-Pod cleanup is lost by skipping deletion here.

Tested: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./environment/kubernetes/...`, `go test ./...` all pass. Added `TestWaitForStop`, which covers Pod-absent and Pod-exists-but-not-running cases; the not-running case blocks for the full timeout without the fix and returns immediately with it.

judge.reason: Both accurately explain the root cause, fix, and testing with nearly identical content and quality, differing mainly in formatting (A uses a code block and headers, B is more prose-based).

original.title: ⚡ [Performance] Use Promise.all for concurrent reference updates in CMS service

output.title: Run reference updates concurrently in the CMS service
output.body:
The `create`, `addReferences`, and `removeReferences` methods in `integrations/cms/service.ts` looped over reference groups with sequential `await` calls, even though each `insertReference`/`removeReference` call is independent I/O. Tested: benchmarked sequential vs. parallel with a mocked 50ms API latency across 4 reference groups — ~202ms sequential vs. ~51ms parallel, about a 75% reduction.

original.title: feat: implement TPC-H benchmark suite

output.title: Add TPC-H benchmark suite for Triplox
output.body:
Adds a Clojure benchmark under `bench/tpch/` that loads TPC-H data via `io.airlift.tpch` and runs all 22 TPC-H queries against Triplox, following the same schema/data-loading/Docker Compose pattern as the AuctionMark benchmark.

What's mechanical
- `Dockerfile`, `deps.edn`, `docker-compose.yml` (~70 lines): standard Clojure image, `rustfs` + `mc` bucket bootstrap, and a `triplox` service wired to `TRIPLOX_STORAGE: remote`, plus a `benchmark` service with `SCALE_FACTOR` (default `0.05`).

Behavior changes
- `tpch/schema.clj` defines the 8 TPC-H tables as Triplox attrs; FK columns (`orders/custkey`, `lineitem/orderkey`, etc.) are `:db.type/ref`.
- `tpch/data.clj` converts each `TpchEntity` to a namespaced-keyword map (`col-name->keyword`), submits in batches of `batch-size` 1000, and fences on a final `[:db/ident :tpch/fence]` transact to block until indexing catches up.
- `tpch/queries.clj` implements all 22 queries as `run-q1`..`run-q22`; subqueries that Datalog can't express in one shot are split into sequential `tc/q` calls with client-side joins/aggregation (e.g. `run-q8`'s market-share ratio), and `IN`-list literals become `or`/`or-join` clauses.
- Queries assume `re-find` (#214), `if` (#215), `year` (#216), `subs` (#217), and `starts-with?` (#218) land in Triplox's Datalog before this runs.
- `tpch/main.clj` reads `TRIPLOX_HOST`/`TRIPLOX_PORT`/`SCALE_FACTOR` from env, loads data, then times and runs every query in `queries/all-queries`, printing row count and ms per query (or the exception message on failure).

Risk: `run-q2` is unfinished — it threads `results` through `filter` and then re-references `results` directly inside the `->>` (dead filter, no actual min-supplycost join), per the "Actually, let's include supplycost..." comment in the code. It currently returns unfiltered rows sorted/limited, not the TPC-H-correct answer.

Not tested: this hasn't been run yet. Before merging, start a Triplox server and run `clojure -M -m tpch.main` from `bench/tpch/` (or `docker compose up`) and confirm all 22 queries execute without errors, especially `run-q2` given the note above.

- `agents/github_agent.py`: `GitHubAgent` creates/lists issues and PRs, searches code, reads repo info, and posts comments via the GitHub REST API.
- `utils/telemetria.py`: OpenTelemetry spans via `span_contextmanager` and `@traceado`, plus `inicializar_telemetria()`; no-ops when the SDK isn't installed.
- `agents/plugin_loader.py`: `PluginLoader` scans directories for `.py` agents and hot-reloads them, instantiating by class name.

- `mcp/cliente_mcp.py`: `TransporteHTTP.conectado` now returns a cached `_conectado` flag instead of issuing an HTTP request on every property access.

output.title: Add up/down block reordering and fix editor media preview bugs
output.body: Editor blocks needed a simple way to move up/down without changing the block contract, and several media preview paths were unreliable: image preview popups were falsely reported as blocked, some browsers left a blank tab after navigating to the object URL, audio play buttons stayed active during playback, and switching audio tracks quickly could surface a stale error. Reordering - `EditorDraftSession.reorderBlockByDelta(blockId, delta)` moves a block by `-1`/`1`, renormalizes every `position` to `0..n-1`, and calls `touchDraft()`. - `renderBlockList` adds a `.block-item-actions` container with move-up/move-down icon buttons, disabled at list boundaries, that call `stopPropagation` before invoking `reorderBlockByDelta` and `updateSummary`. - `.editor-layout`'s sidebar column widens from `minmax(280px, 360px)` to `minmax(322px, 414px)` to fit the new buttons; `.block-item-row` gets `min-width: 0` and `.icon-btn` gets `flex-shrink: 0` so the row doesn't crush them. Image preview - `openAssetImage` calls `window.open('', '_blank')` (dropping `noopener`/`noreferrer`) synchronously before any async asset lookup — Chrome 88+ returns `null` from `window.open` when those flags are set even though the tab opens, and the async lookup was breaking the gesture context. - If `previewWindow.location.replace(objectUrl)` throws, it now falls back to injecting an `` into the popup document instead of leaving a blank tab. Audio preview - `playAssetAudio` tracks the active playback in `previewAudioPlayback` with `onStart`/`onEnded`/`onError`/`onInterrupted` hooks and a new `finalizePreviewAudio(reason)` helper, so play state reflects reality instead of staying "playing" after it ends or errors. - A `_previewPlayRequestId` counter makes a superseded `playAssetAudio` call return `{ ok: false, reason: 'superseded' }` instead of emitting stale error feedback when the user switches tracks rapidly. Also in the diff: `getBlockDeletePolicy`, `getOptionDeletePolicy`, and `getSwitchImpact` route destructive block/option deletes and answer-type switches through a new `.confirm-modal` dialog when typed content or attachments would be lost; `switchQuestionInputTypeWithImpactPolicy` and `removeQuestionOptionWithPolicy` return `confirm-switch-required` until the caller passes `confirmSwitch: true`. Viewer: `getInputHelperText` for `multiple_choice` now reads `responseConfig.selectionMode` — `'single'` (default) shows "Choose one option only.", `'multi'` shows "Choose one or more options." (previously always the multi-select copy). original.title: fix: install centaur tool CLI shims in sandbox

output.title: Install centaur tool CLI shims in sandbox
output.body:
Live asbx pods run `centaur-agent:main-sha-412d4fc`. api-rs invokes `install-tool-shims --copy-tools` from tools-bootstrap, but the deployed script ignores `--copy-tools`, publishes no packages into `/app/tools`, and `centaur-tools list` comes back empty. This adds the shim installer to the sandbox image, wires it into the entrypoint, and carries the tool-discovery/routing changes it depends on.

Sandbox shims
- `install_tool_shims.py` is copied into the image as `/usr/local/bin/install-tool-shims`; `entrypoint.sh` runs it whenever `TOOL_DIRS`/`TOOLS_PATH`/`TOOLS_OVERLAY_PATH` is set and adds `/opt/centaur` plus each tool dir's parent to `PYTHONPATH` (`CENTAUR_TOOL_PYTHONPATH`).
- `_copy_published_tools` implements `--copy-tools`, publishing nested tool packages into the target dir and skipping duplicates by name — the gap that left `/app/tools` empty on `main-sha-412d4fc`.

Tool discovery / secrets
- `ToolManager` gains a discovery gate (`_missing_required_secret_env`, `secret_env_refs`): a tool is skipped when a required secret's env var is unset under the `env` secret source, logged as `tool_skipped_missing_secrets`; no-op under `onepassword*`.
- The tool-server sidecar has no secrets of its own, so the API now passes it an allowlist via `CENTAUR_AVAILABLE_SECRET_REFS` (`kubernetes.py:_build_tool_server_container`); without it, the sidecar falls back to `gate_on_missing_secrets=False` (fail open).
- `app.py` re-adds `app.include_router(tool_manager.create_rest_router())`, restoring the API's own `/tools/*` routes.
- `call.sh`'s new `tool_request()` falls back from the tool-server URL to the API URL on `transport_error`/404/405.

Other changes in this branch, by area
- API: `workflow_engine.py` adds `_ensure_app_state_db_pool`, backfilling `app.state.db_pool` in `_run_handler` without overwriting an existing pool.
- Slackbot: `normalize.ts` treats Slack `im`/`mpim` events as mentions, so DMs no longer need a text mention to be actionable.
